기록·스크립트: B 약 16초, C 약 80초, D 약 14분. Codex·agy 교차 리뷰를 받아 수정했으며, 학습자 파일럿은 아니다). 각 트랙의 질문의 나머지 절반은 대부분 

이어서 시험 실행했다(A①②③, B①, C①②③④, D②③⑤). C②는 새 데이터셋(CELLxGENE Cross-sectional)으로, C③은 Geneformer V1-10M 미세조정(Mac)과 V2-104M 미세조정(Colab A100; Mac에서는 비현실적)으로, C④는 scGPT whole-human zero-shot 임베딩으로 실행했다. ChemBERTa 미세조정은 하지 않았다. 필요한 열은 모두 있었으나 트랙 C의 세부 라벨(cell.type.fine)은 pbmc_sub.h5ad에 없어서 노트북 04/01의 하위표본 추출을 재현해 붙여야 했다. 질문에 필요한 라벨, 좌표, 열이 캐시에 있는지는 제안서 단계에서 직접 확인한다. 트랙 E는 후보 5편을 

조사하고 TraitGym 한 편을 L1(점수 → 지표 계산 수준) + L3로 

시험 실행했다. 본문의 Mendelian zero-shot 주장 7개와 표·그림 일부(Table 1·S4·S8·S9, Figure 5, 보충 그림 S7·S8; 그림은 순서 수준)를 캐시와 대조했고, 점수 생성 단계와 나머지 표·그림은 재현하거나 확인하지 못했다. 학습자의 트랙 E는 본인이 고른 논문이며, 논문·데이터·계산 비용 확인이 선행 조건이다. 각 트랙의 MVP는 위 질문 중 하나를 사전 지정 비교 하나로 줄인 것이다. 확장(다른 assay, 더 큰 모델, 새 데이터)은 MVP가 끝난 뒤에만 한다. 새 데이터나 모델이 필요하면 제안서에 파일, 출처, 크기, 라이선스를 적고 승인을 받는다.

records.content:
Pineau et al.(arXiv:2003.12206 초록)은 재현성을 "같은 코드와 데이터(가능하면)로 논문에 보고된 것과 비슷한 결과를 얻는 것"으로 설명한다. 이 프로토콜은 그 정의를 주장 단위로 좁힌다.

논문 고르기 (

논문 노트 템플릿과 3-pass 읽기로): 아래 4가지 조건을 모두 만족하는 논문을 고른다. ① 핵심 주장이 한 문장이다. ② 코드·데이터·가중치가 공개되어 있고 라이선스를 확인했다. ③ 계산이 16~20시간 안에 들어간다(🟢 Mac / 🟡 Colab). ④ 재현할 주장 단위(표 한 칸 또는 그림 하나)를 특정할 수 있다. 

reading_list의 ✅ 논문에서 고르되 코드 공개 여부는 직접 확인한다. 작성자가 4가지 조건을 후보 5편에 적용해 본 

후보 조사가 있다. 예시이며 정답이 아니다.

재현 수준을 정한다: L1 숫자 재현(공개 코드·가중치로 해당 수치가 허용 오차 안), L2 재구현(핵심 파이프라인을 직접 구현해 L1과 비교), L3 변형 검증(분할, baseline, ablation을 바꿔 주장이 유지되는지)이 있다. 권장은 L1에 L3 하나를 더하는 것이다.

허용 오차를 주 재현 결과를 보기 전에 정의한다. 논문이 구간을 주면 그것을 쓴다. 주지 않으면 원 코드를 시드만 바꿔 실행한 변동을 먼저 재서 기록한 뒤(주 결과를 보기 전에) 그 변동으로 정한다. “±0.02” 같은 값을 결과를 본 뒤에 고르지 않는다.

편차 기록(deviation log): 데이터 버전, 전처리, 환경, 시드, 논문에 없던 세부를 날짜와 함께 적는다.

재현이 안 될 때: 원인 후보(데이터 버전, 전처리, 평가 코드, 누출 가능성, 시드)를 하나씩 점검하고 저자 코드와 비교한다. "재현 실패"는 유효한 결과이지만 원인을 확인하지 못했으면 그렇게 쓴다. 논문이 틀렸다고 단정하지 않는다.

보고서는 

report_template를 쓰되 §1에 재현 수준과 허용 오차를, §5에 "논문의 주장과 내가 확인한 것의 차이"를 둔다.

제안서 템플릿 → 

템플릿 노트북에서 시작 →

제출 전 점검표 →

예시: 템플릿 노트북의 실제 실행 결과로 채운 제안서와 보고서(트랙 A, 짧은 형태)다. 형식을 보여 주기 위한 것이며 결론을 일반화하지 않는다.

B~D 시험 실행 기록: 트랙 B·C·D의 MVP를 템플릿 구조로 옮겨 실행한 기록과 스크립트다(템플릿에서 바꿔야 했던 부분, 대조 정의, 결과). 트랙 E는 

TraitGym 시험 실행에서 다뤘다.

질문의 나머지 절반 시험 실행 기록: 위 MVP에서 빠졌던 질문(A①②③, B①, C①②③④, D②③⑤)을 같은 방식으로 실행한 기록과 스크립트 11개다(C③의 V2-104M 미세조정만 Colab A100에서 학습). 새로 내려받은 것은 MoleculeNet CSV 3개, CELLxGENE H5AD 1개(150 MB), scGPT 소스 .py 26개와 whole-human 체크포인트(약 207 MB)뿐이며 모두 승인 후 받았다(설치 없음).

템플릿 노트북은 ✏️ 셀(설정, 결정 규칙, 한계)만 바꾸고 나머지 구조를 유지한다. 트랙 A(ProteinGym 변이) 전용이므로 다른 트랙에서는 데이터 로딩, 특징 추출, 분할 키(군집 단위), B0 함수를 교체해야 한다. 실행 기록은 .cache/capstone_runs/<RUN_NAME>/(git 제외)에 쓴다.

그룹 부트스트랩 구간은 계산하지 않았다. 길이 55 단백질을 블록 10으로 나누면 블록이 6개뿐이고 position-block의 test는 2개 블록이다. 군집 2개를 복원추출하면 가능한 재표본이 3가지뿐이라 구간이 무의미하다. 노트북은 모든 시드의 test 군집이 MIN_TEST_GROUPS(8) 이상일 때만 구간을 계산하도록 막아 두었고, 구간 코드는 합성 데이터(40개 군집)로 따로 점검했다(같은 정확도면 구간이 0을 포함하고, 한쪽이 훨씬 정확하면 포함하지 않는다). 시드 5개는 같은 1,008개 변이에서 분할을 다시 뽑은 것이라 test 집합이 겹친다. 독립 반복이 아니라 분할 민감도를 보는 것이다.

시연용으로 정한 결정 규칙(“Δ 시드 평균 ≥ 0.02, 이긴 시드 ≥ 4/5, 구간을 계산할 수 있으면 하한 > 0”)에 따라 판정은 **‘지지되지 않음’**이다(Δ 평균 −0.065, 0/5, 구간 없음). 블록 크기 민감도(3 / 5 / 10, test 군집 최소 4 / 3 / 2개)에서 Δ(probe−B2)는 −0.064 / −0.013 / −0.065다. 읽는 법은 다음과 같다.

random 분할에서 probe와 B2의 차이는 작고(+0.010) 시드마다 부호가 바뀌어(4/5) 방향을 확정하지 못했다. 이 분할에서는 test 위치가 train에 100% 들어 있다. position-block에서는 probe가 B1·B2보다 낮았고 5개 시드 모두에서 B2에 졌다.

사전학습의 기여(probe − 무작위 초기화)는 random 분할에서 뚜렷하지만(+0.167) position-block에서는 +0.012로 방향을 확정하지 못했다(3/5). 무작위 초기화를 시드마다 새로 만들어서 얻은 값이다. 한 개의 초기화(시드 0)로 비교했을 때는 +0.063처럼 보였다. 대조군이 하나뿐이면 그 한 초기화의 운이 결론이 될 수 있다.

B0(가장 가까운 train 위치의 평균)는 새 위치에서 작동하지 않는다(−0.04). 블록 안 위치가 모두 같은 가장자리 위치로 매핑되어 예측이 상수에 가깝고, 시드 하나에서는 Spearman이 정의되지 않았다(NaN으로 기록하고 제외).

음성 진단의 시드 평균은 0 근처지만 position-block에서는 test 군집이 2개뿐이라 시드 하나의 |ρ|가 0.3까지 갔다. 이 진단은 누출이 없다는 증명이 아니다. 평균이 0에서 멀면 조사하는 신호로 쓴다.

한 assay, 8M, Ridge만, 시드 5개의 결과다. 조건부 구간조차 없다.

Colab T4 재실행 (2026-11-06, 1회, 93초; Python 3.13, torch 2.14.1, scikit-learn 1.6.1, pandas 2.2.3, numpy 2.4.6. Mac은 scikit-learn 1.9.1, pandas 3.1.1, numpy 2.5.4): 같은 노트북이 오류 없이 끝났고 시드별 ρ 60개가 Mac과 2×10⁻⁴ 안에서 같았다(정의되지 않은 값 1개도 같다). 위 표와 판정은 같다. 달랐던 것은 블록 크기 민감도의 블록 3이다. Δ(probe−B2)의 시드 평균이 −0.079(이긴 시드 0/5)로, Mac의 −0.064(2/5)와 달랐다. 블록 5는 −0.011(2/5)로 Mac의 −0.013(2/5)과, 블록 10은 −0.065(0/5)로 Mac과 같았다. 라이브러리 버전과 장치만 다르고 원인은 가려내지 못했다. 민감도 숫자는 환경에 따라 달라질 수 있는 값으로 읽는다.

루브릭은 8개 차원(질문, 사전 등록, 데이터·누출, baseline·대조군, 평가·불확실성, 재현성, 해석·한계, 책임성) × 0~3점이다. 증거를 적고 매기며, 자동 상한(red flag)이 있다. 설정을 test로 골랐는데 그 test에서 평가한 결과를 주 결과로 낸 경우("사전 고정"이라고 썼는지와 무관하게; 별도 test가 없으면 탐색적 결과로 표시), 누출을 재지 않고 "없음"이라고 쓴 경우, 서술과 출력이 다른 경우 등이 해당한다. 합격(합계 ≥16, 0점 차원 없음, red flag 없음)과 전문가 수준 체크포인트(합계 ≥20, 모든 차원 ≥2, red flag 없음)는 이 과정이 제안하는 임의의 기준이다. 

점검표는 모듈 01~06에서 실제로 틀렸던 것을 모은 것이다.

모듈 04~06에서 한 방식을 일반화했다. 읽기 전용으로 두 모델 이상에 보내고(

프롬프트 템플릿), 지적을 하나씩 코드와 출력으로 검증한다. 모델 둘에게 같은 묶음을 보내는 것만으로 검토가 독립적인 것은 아니다. 누구에게 무엇을 보냈는지, 검토자 사이에 정보가 공유되었는지를 기록한다. 모델 접근이 없으면 사람 검토로, 또는 하루 뒤에 점검표만 보고 처음 읽는 사람처럼 하는 분리된 자기 점검(시각과 발견 항목 기록)으로 대신하고, 독립성이 약하다는 한계를 보고서에 적는다. 이 과정에서 검토는 매번 실제 버그를 찾았지만(예: 서열 중복이 분할에 걸림, 표준화가 내부 CV에 섞임, PCA 표본이 길이순 앞부분) 일부 지적은 오해였다(예: 전체 데이터로 상수 열을 빼는 것). 검토자에게 확인하지 못한 것과 중간에 틀렸다가 고친 것을 알려 주면 거짓 양성이 줄어든다. 수용·기각 근거를 표로 남기고(보고서 부록), 고친 뒤에는 노트북을 처음부터 다시 실행한다.

records.content:
다음 문장에서 문제를 찾아 보자. 모두 이 과정에서 실제로 있었거나 있을 법한 사례를 바탕으로 만들었다.

Q1. “5-fold random 교차검증에서 ESM-2 probe가 위치를 쓰지 않는 단순 baseline보다 0.10 높았으므로 ESM-2는 변이 효과를 잘 예측한다.”

답random 분할에서는 같은 위치의 다른 치환이 train에 있어 위치 효과를 쓰는 baseline(B2)과의 차이가 작아질 수 있다(템플릿 데모: probe − B2 = +0.010으로 방향을 확정하지 못했고, 위치를 쓰지 않는 B1과는 +0.112). 위치를 쓰지 않는 B1과만 비교했거나 새 위치를 예측하는 분할을 쓰지 않았다면 "새 위치를 예측한다"는 주장을 할 수 없다. 분할이 막은 경로와 막지 못한 경로를 숫자(test 위치가 train에 있는 비율)로 보여야 한다.

Q2. “층 4, 8, 12를 비교해 test Spearman이 가장 높은 층 8을 사용했다. 설정은 사전에 고정했다.”

답test 결과로 층을 골라 그 test 점수를 주 결과로 보고한 것은 "사전 고정"이라고 썼든 아니든 루브릭의 red flag다(차원 2·5 상한 1점). 별도 test가 없다면 *탐색적 결과*로 표시해야 한다. 사전 고정이었다면 층을 미리 정하고 나머지는 *민감도*로 보고해야 하며, 선택이 필요하면 학습 안 검증 분할(바깥과 같은 방식)로 골라야 한다. 모듈 04의 층 선택(0.18 차이)과 모듈 06의 LoRA 민감도가 같은 문제를 보여 준다.

Q3. “scaffold 분할을 썼으므로 train–test 누출은 없다.”

답분할 이름은 누출이 없다는 것을 보장하지 않는다. 모듈 05에서 scaffold 분할에서도 Lipophilicity test의 26%가 train에 Tanimoto ≥ 0.7인 분자를 가졌다(최근접 유사도 중앙값 0.57). 분할 후 test→train 유사도를 측정해 보고하고, 막지 못한 경로는 더 엄격한 분할이나 층화로 점검한다.

Q4. “BBBP에서 모든 폴드의 예측을 합쳐 AUROC를 구했다. 층 0의 <s> 표현은 0.46이어서 우연보다 약간 나쁘다.”

답폴드마다 다른 모델의 점수 척도를 하나로 섞으면, 상수 예측도 폴드별 평균 예측의 차이 때문에 0.5에서 벗어난다. 폴드별 AUROC를 구해 평균하면 이 상수 표현은 정확히 0.500이다(모듈 05). 같은 이유로 풀링한 지표는 폴드 간 보정 차이에 민감하다.

Q5. “시드 3개 평균에서 LoRA(0.41)가 probe(0.56)보다 낮았으므로 LoRA는 이 과제에 쓸모가 없다.”

답고정된 하나의 설정(r=8, lr 1e-3, 5 에폭)과 시드 3개, 8M 모델, 검증 기반 선택 없음의 결과일 뿐이다. 같은 노트북의 민감도에서 LoRA는 설정에 따라 0.29~0.50으로 흔들렸고, 35M·시드 2개에서는 순서가 달랐다(모듈 06). "이 고정 설정에서는 이기지 못했다"가 데이터가 지지하는 서술이다.

Q6. “검토 모델이 지적한 12개 항목을 모두 반영했다.”

답지적을 검증 없이 모두 수용한 것은 루브릭의 red flag다. 검토자는 실제 버그를 찾지만 오해도 한다(모듈 06: 전체 데이터로 상수 열을 빼는 것은 어떤 예측도 바꾸지 않아 누출이 아니다). 각 지적을 코드와 출력으로 확인해 수용·기각 근거를 표로 남기고, 고친 뒤 처음부터 재실행해 실행본과 제출 코드가 같은지 확인해야 한다.

records.content:
English translation. AI-assisted translation of the 

Korean original. The Korean original is authoritative and may be newer. Links to pages without an English version open the Korean original.

What this record is: Track A runs directly as the 

template notebook, but B–D only pointed to starting points. This record is what the people who made the course did: they chose an MVP (one pre-specified comparison) for each track, moved it into the template structure (preregistration → provenance → data inspection → unit and leakage → baselines → evaluation → controls → sensitivity), and actually ran it.

It is not a learner pilot. The time a learner would need and where they would get stuck were not measured.

It is not a real preregistration. The design and the results were made at about the same time, and it cannot be proven that the decision rules were set before the results were seen. It is in the same position as the 

track A example, which is meant to show the format.

Each comparison is a single run. Do not generalize the results below to “DNA LMs / single-cell FMs / chemical LMs are …”.

It received Codex and agy cross-review (see the “Cross-review” section at the bottom). Each point was checked against the code and incorporated, and for the points that were not incorporated the reason is given.

The other half of the questions that this record left as “not done” was run next in 

Dry-Run Record of the “Other Half of the Question” for Tracks A–D (2026-11-09) (2026-11-09).

The environment is a Mac (CPU/MPS) and the repository .venv, and there are no new downloads (only the caches that modules 03, 04 and 05 had downloaded were used). records.content:
Setup (fixed): TraitGym mendelian_traits_matched_9 (3,380 variants, 338 positives, 9 matched controls per 1 positive = 338 match_groups, 19 chromosomes). The metric is AUPRC. The sign of each score was fixed before looking at the data (LLR −, conservation +). Δ = AUPRC(model) − AUPRC(baseline). The decision rule is ‘supported’ if all three of the following conditions hold: the mean of the per-chromosome Δ (the 14 chromosomes with ≥ 5 positives) is 0.02 or more; the number of chromosomes with Δ > 0 is 10/14 or more; and the lower bound of the 95% interval of the match_group-level paired bootstrap (500 resamples) is greater than 0. The per-score permutation null has 1,000 resamples.

Data inspection (assert): The score files and the variant table have the same number of rows, there is no NaN, each group has exactly 1 positive, each group lies within one chromosome, and there are no duplicate variants. All of them passed.

AUPRC: The permutation p is, for each score, a comparison against the pooled-AUPRC distribution of 1,000 shuffles of that score’s own values within match_group. The null mean is 0.100–0.102, the 95% quantile is 0.103–0.112, and the minimum of p is 0.001.

Primary comparison NT LLR − phyloP-241m: pooled Δ −0.571 [−0.618, −0.519], chromosome-mean Δ −0.561, 0/14 chromosomes with Δ > 0, so it is not supported. The secondary comparison Evo2-7B LLR − phyloP-241m has Δ −0.293 [−0.348, −0.231], 1/14, and is not supported. Both comparisons were pre-specified, and no multiple-comparison correction was made.

Controls: The negative control shuffles the model score within match_group, and its AUPRC is 0.096 (the null mean of NT LLR is 0.102). The positive control is Evo2-7B LLR vs TSS distance only, with pooled Δ +0.266 [+0.213, +0.314], chromosome-mean Δ +0.231, 13/14, so it is ‘supported’.

Sensitivity (one at a time): Changing the baseline to phyloP-100v and to phastCons-43p is still not supported in both cases (Δ −0.550 / −0.394). Changing the minimum number of positives per chromosome to 3 and to 10 gives Δ > 0 in only 1 of 17 and 0 of 10 chromosomes, respectively.

It matches the AUPRC of module 03 notebook 02 (NT 0.103, Evo2-7B 0.38, phyloP-241m 0.67, TSS 0.115). The permutation p did not match before the cross-review of this record. Notebook 02 used a single null distribution for all scores (the values obtained by shuffling the within-group ranks 0…9), giving NT 0.34 and TSS 0.006. The permutation distribution of the observed statistic (pooled AUPRC) is obtained by shuffling each score’s own values, so notebook 02 was fixed in the same way (see “Cross-review” below), and it is now NT 0.41 (this script gives 0.445 because the seed is different; Monte Carlo standard error about 0.015) and TSS 0.001.

What was changed from the template: This track has no training (zero-shot). make_split, fit_predict, PRED, Ridge and the random-init model are not needed; the per-seed Δ slot was moved to the per-chromosome Δ, and MIN_TEST_GROUPS to MIN_POS_CHROM and the number of match_groups. decide() could be used as it is. The negative control is not “shuffling labels” but “shuffling scores within groups”.

Where it got stuck / cautions: ① The question said “to change the split unit, first check whether coordinates exist”, and the variant table had chrom, pos and match_group, so the chromosome unit was possible. ② The AUPRC of a chromosome with only 2–8 positives fluctuates a lot (so the minimum number of positives was pre-specified). ③ The directly computed NT LLR covers only 210 chr1 variants (21 positives), which is unsuitable for an MVP, so the provided score was used.

What cannot be said: It is only a comparison on this variant set and this metric, and it does not apply to DNA LMs in general or to other diseases and complex traits. The model variant and the window length of the NT score provided by TraitGym were not checked†.

What was not done: The other half of the question (“how much does the gain of the NT probe depend on the layer choice and the size of the 6-mer baseline?”) was not run in this record, because the NT embeddings were not in the cache. It was later run in 

B① of second_halves.en.md by computing the embeddings anew (about 6 minutes).

records.content:
Setup (fixed): A 10,400-cell subsample of Wilk 2020 PBMC, 13 donors, leave-one-donor-out by donor. The head is logistic regression (C = 1 fixed; centering, L2 normalization and standardization are fitted only on the training donors). However, the PCA (HVG, 50) baseline of the primary comparison is a transductive setting in which HVG selection, scaling and PCA are fitted (without labels) on all cells including the held-out donor (the same way as module 04 notebook 02). This favors PCA, and there is no such fitting for the Geneformer embeddings. Fold-wise fitting is examined separately in the sensitivity analysis. The primary comparison is V2-104M <cls> L-2 vs PCA (HVG, 50), with 13 coarse labels. The metrics are the pooled macro-F1 (donor-level bootstrap, 1,000 resamples) and the per-donor balanced accuracy. The decision rule is: mean of the per-donor balanced-accuracy Δ ≥ 0.02, donors with Δ > 0 ≥ 9/13, and the lower bound of the macro-F1 Δ interval > 0.

Where the cache blocked: pbmc_sub.h5ad has no fine-grained label (cell.type.fine), and the cell names were also changed to cell0…, so they cannot be linked to the original (obs: donor, disease, label, cell_type_cxg, n_counts). balanced_subsample in notebook 04/01 (seed 0, 800 per donor) is deterministic, so it was applied again to wilk2020_pbmc.h5ad; after confirming that the donor, coarse label and cxg label of all 10,400 cells agree, the 20 fine-grained labels were attached (the script asserts this). There are no new downloads. PCA (HVG) was not in the cache, so it was built by the same procedure as notebook 04/02 (7 seconds).

Primary comparison V2 − PCA: macro-F1 Δ −0.018 [−0.031, −0.009], per-donor balanced-accuracy Δ −0.036, donors 3/13, so it is not supported. The control, the pretraining effect (V1 − V1 random initialization), has pooled macro-F1 Δ +0.198 [+0.182, +0.223], mean per-donor balanced-accuracy Δ +0.183, 13/13, so it is ‘supported’. Unless stated otherwise, the Δ below is the pooled macro-F1 Δ, the same as the interval, and the decision rule looks together at the mean and the number of wins of the per-donor balanced-accuracy Δ and at this interval.

Sensitivity (one at a time): If PCA is fitted per fold, leaving out the held-out donor (centering and L2 normalization applied the same as in the primary comparison), Δ is −0.015 [−0.031, −0.004], balanced-accuracy Δ −0.030, 3/13. If the head is changed to kNN (k = 15), Δ is −0.036 [−0.064, −0.018], balanced-accuracy Δ −0.090, 0/13 (the same as the zero-shot numbers of module 04 notebook 02: PCA 0.847, V2 0.811). If the labels are changed to the 20 fine-grained ones, Δ is −0.079 [−0.097, −0.062], balanced-accuracy Δ −0.103, 0/13 (PCA 0.824, V2 0.744). All of them are not supported.

Reading: The supervised head narrowed the gap (from kNN −0.036 to logistic −0.018) but stayed below PCA, and the gap grew as the labels became finer. It is the result for one dataset and 1 head hyperparameter (C = 1).

What was changed from the template: The unit is the donor instead of the seed (the split is deterministic), and logistic regression and macro-F1 are used instead of Ridge and Spearman. The negative control is “shuffling the training labels”, and for the random-init control the V1 random-init embeddings in the cache were used.

Cautions: ⓪ The logistic head in this script has max_iter=300, while the C②③④ scripts of 

Dry-Run Record of the “Other Half of the Question” for Tracks A–D (2026-11-09) written afterward use max_iter=3000. For that reason the balanced accuracy of the same PCA baseline is written as 0.841 here and 0.842 there (the pooled macro-F1 is 0.856 in both; no effect on the verdict). Also, the “PCA per fold” here (0.835) is the one in which only PCA is fitted per fold, while the “strict per fold” there (0.841) is a different procedure in which even the filter, HVG and scaling are fitted on the training folds. ① HVG selection was done with all the cells (a limitation that remains even when PCA is fitted per fold). ② The disease status overlaps completely with the donors (7 COVID, 6 normal). ③ With max_iter = 300, the logistic convergence warning appeared 13 times. When re-run with a copy in which only max_iter was raised to 3000, there were no warnings and the numbers above were the same (only the negative control changed from 0.068 to 0.069). The warnings come from joblib worker processes, so they are printed regardless of the warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") at the top of the script (also 13 times in the re-run after the review). The “y_pred contains classes not in y_true” warning of balanced_accuracy_score also appears. It occurs when a cell type that is not in one donor’s test set is predicted, and the balanced accuracy averages only over the types that actually exist in that donor. ④ The per-fold PCA also did HVG selection with all the cells.

Not done (in the MVP of this document): A new dataset, fine-tuning, and other models such as scGPT. Later, in 

Dry-Run Record of the “Other Half of the Question” for Tracks A–D (2026-11-09), label granularity (C①), a new dataset (C②), Geneformer V1-10M fine-tuning (C③) and scGPT zero-shot embeddings (C④) were run, and V2-104M fine-tuning was run separately on a Colab A100 (C③-V2).

records.content:
All three tracks could run the MVP to the end using only the cache, with no new downloads. There was one blocker (the fine-grained labels of track C), and it was resolved by deterministic reproduction.

The template notebook does not work as it is, but its structure can be moved over. What changed was only the data loading, the features, the split and unit (from seeds to chromosomes, donors and repeats), and the metric. decide() and the order “preregistration → provenance → inspection → controls → sensitivity” were used as they were. For comparisons without training, as in track B, the make_split/fit_predict interface does not fit.

The controls had to be redefined for each track. The negative control was “shuffling scores within groups” in B, “shuffling the training labels” in C and “shuffling labels” in D, and the positive control that shows the decision rule can output ‘supported’ was “Evo2-7B vs TSS distance only” in B and “pretraining vs random initialization” in C and D. Without these positive controls we could not have told whether the “not supported” of the three tracks was a bias of the rule.

That all three primary comparisons came out “not supported” is partly because of the choice of question (asking whether an FM beats a strong baseline). It is not a new conclusion, but in the same direction as modules 03, 04 and 05.

records.content:
The full diffs of commit 1999904 (Module 02 ESMFold Colab), f406cbd (modules 05–07 Colab) and df8e368 (this folder) were shown read-only to Codex (gpt-6.1-terra) and agy (gemini-4-argon-low) for review (Codex 6 points, agy 8 points). Each point was checked against the code.

Incorporated

B permutation p (Codex, incorporated): The null distribution was built from ranks (0…9) unrelated to the score and was used in common for all scores. It was changed to shuffle each score’s own values within the group (the table above). The p values that changed are NT LLR 0.338 → 0.445 and TSS distance only 0.006 → 0.001, and the other results (AUPRC, primary and secondary comparisons, controls, sensitivity) are unchanged. Module 03 notebook 02 had the same rank-based null distribution, so it was fixed in the same way and re-run. The p-values over all variants went NT 0.34 → 0.41, HyenaDNA 0.53 → 0.63, Caduceus 0.92 → 0.93 and TSS 0.006 → 0.001. The chr1 subset differed greatly. For the directly computed NT LLR, the 1-frame p went 0.035 → 0.109, the 6-frame mean 0.138 → 0.289, and the 6-frame × forward/reverse 0.106 → 0.273, and for the public NT LLR 0.007 → 0.063. On chr1 all the earlier p-values were too small (less conservative). The AUPRC and the bootstrap intervals are unchanged.

Transductive fitting of the primary PCA baseline in C (Codex, agy; disclosure strengthened): The code already did this and the comments said so, but the README’s setup paragraph did not. It is now stated in the setup. The primary comparison itself is the same setting as module 04 notebook 02, so it was not changed, and fold-wise fitting had already been run as a sensitivity analysis.

The fold-wise PCA sensitivity in C was changing two factors (Codex, incorporated): The fold-wise PCA lacked the training-mean centering and the row L2 normalization. It was aligned with the primary comparison and re-run (Δ −0.017 → −0.015; the conclusion is the same, and all the other numbers were the same as in the earlier run).

Added the hash of wilk2020_pbmc.h5ad to the provenance of C (Codex): It is the file used to reconstruct the fine-grained labels.

MIN_GROUPS in B was only defined and not used (Codex, agy): An assert was added. The selection of the TraitGym snapshot (the first entry of iterdir()) now sorts only the directories and stops if there is not exactly one (agy).

Notation (agy): It was not shown whether the control and sensitivity Δ in C were the pooled macro-F1 or the balanced accuracy, and B’s positive control had a pooled interval attached to the chromosome-mean Δ. Both are now distinguished. The numbers of bootstrap and permutation resamples of B are also given.

What the D negative control evaluates (Codex): It is the RMSE of a model trained on shuffled labels and compared with the original labels. The code was left as it is (only a comment was added, AST identical), and it is stated in the table header and the comment. It was not re-run.

Not incorporated

decide() exempts the interval condition when ci is None (agy): This is the design of the template notebook, and DECISION_RULE says “when an interval can be computed”. The D script has MIN_TEST_GROUPS = 8, and when only the first part of the script was re-run, the minimum number of test clusters in every split was 162–840, so it did not trigger in this run.

decide() uses len(deltas) < MIN_WINS as the lower bound on valid units (agy): This is inherited from the template. If this condition is hit, it cannot be ‘supported’ anyway, and only the label changes to ‘cannot judge’. The MIN_POS_CHROM=10 sensitivity case that agy cited does not call decide().

LogisticRegression has no random_state, and the warnings are hidden so the 13 warnings cannot be seen (agy): The lbfgs solver does not use random_state. The warnings are printed by joblib workers, and ConvergenceWarning was seen 13 times even in the re-run after the review.

The weights_only comment in the ESMFold notebook (agy): from_pretrained in transformers 5.22.1 defaults to weights_only: bool = True, and .bin files are read through the torch.load(weights_only=True) path (checked in modeling_utils.py). The comment is correct.

The two Colab commits (1999904, f406cbd): Neither reviewer pointed out a problem. The outputs of the notebooks were empty, so the reviewers could not recompute the numbers of the Colab runs — this part was not independently verified.

설정(고정): TraitGym mendelian_traits_matched_9(변이 3,380, 양성 338, 양성 1개당 매칭된 대조 9개 = match_group 338개, 염색체 19개). 지표는 AUPRC다. 점수의 부호는 데이터를 보기 전에 규정했다(LLR −, 보존 +). Δ = AUPRC(모델) − AUPRC(baseline)이다. 결정 규칙은 다음 세 조건을 모두 만족하면 '지지’다. 염색체별 Δ(양성 ≥ 5인 14개)의 평균이 0.02 이상이고, Δ > 0인 염색체가 10/14 이상이며, match_group 단위 짝지은 부트스트랩(500회) 95% 구간 하한이 0보다 크다. 점수별 순열 귀무분포는 1,000회다.

데이터 점검(assert): 점수 파일과 변이표의 행 수가 일치하고, NaN이 없고, 그룹당 양성이 정확히 1개이고, 그룹이 한 염색체 안에 있고, 변이 중복이 없다. 모두 통과했다.

AUPRC: 순열 p는 점수마다 그 점수의 값을 match_group 안에서 섞은 1,000회의 풀링 AUPRC 분포와 비교한 것이다. 귀무 평균은 0.100~0.102, 95% 분위수는 0.103~0.112이고 p의 최솟값은 0.001이다.

주 비교 NT LLR − phyloP-241m: 풀링 Δ −0.571 [−0.618, −0.519], 염색체 평균 Δ −0.561, Δ > 0인 염색체 0/14이므로 지지되지 않는다. 보조 비교 Evo2-7B LLR − phyloP-241m는 Δ −0.293 [−0.348, −0.231], 1/14이며 지지되지 않는다. 두 비교를 모두 사전 지정했고 다중 비교 보정은 하지 않았다.

대조: 음성은 모델 점수를 match_group 안에서 섞은 것으로, AUPRC가 0.096이다(NT LLR의 귀무 평균 0.102). 양성은 Evo2-7B LLR vs TSS 거리만이며, 풀링 Δ +0.266 [+0.213, +0.314], 염색체 평균 Δ +0.231, 13/14라 '지지’다.

민감도(한 번에 하나): baseline을 phyloP-100v와 phastCons-43p로 바꿔도 모두 지지되지 않는다(Δ −0.550 / −0.394). 염색체 기준 양성 수를 3과 10으로 바꾸면 각각 17개 중 1개, 10개 중 0개만 Δ > 0이다.

모듈 03 노트북 02의 AUPRC(NT 0.103, Evo2-7B 0.38, phyloP-241m 0.67, TSS 0.115)와 일치한다. 순열 p는 이 기록의 교차 리뷰 전에는 일치하지 않았다. 노트북 02가 모든 점수에 하나의 귀무분포(그룹 안의 순위 0…9를 섞은 값)를 써서 NT 0.34, TSS 0.006이었다. 관측한 통계량(풀링 AUPRC)의 순열 분포는 점수마다 값을 섞은 것이므로 노트북 02도 같은 방식으로 고쳤고(아래 “교차 리뷰”), 지금은 NT 0.41(이 스크립트는 시드가 달라 0.445; 몬테카를로 표준오차 약 0.015), TSS 0.001이다.

템플릿에서 바꾼 것: 이 트랙은 학습이 없다(zero-shot). make_split, fit_predict, PRED, Ridge, 무작위 초기화 모델이 필요 없고, 시드별 Δ 자리를 염색체별 Δ로, MIN_TEST_GROUPS를 MIN_POS_CHROM과 match_group 수로 옮겼다. decide()는 그대로 쓸 수 있었다. 음성 대조는 "라벨 섞기"가 아니라 "그룹 내 점수 섞기"다.

막힌 곳 / 주의: ① 질문이 "분할 단위를 바꾸려면 좌표가 있는지 먼저 확인"이라고 했는데, 변이표에 chrom·pos·match_group이 있어 염색체 단위가 가능했다. ② 양성이 2~8개뿐인 염색체의 AUPRC는 매우 흔들린다(그래서 최소 양성 수를 사전 지정했다). ③ 직접 계산한 NT LLR은 chr1 변이 210개(양성 21개)뿐이라 MVP로는 부적합하므로 제공 점수를 썼다.

말할 수 없는 것: 이 변이 집합과 이 지표에서의 비교일 뿐이며 DNA LM 전체나 다른 질병·복합 형질에는 해당하지 않는다. TraitGym 제공 NT 점수의 모델 변형과 창 길이는 확인하지 않았다†.

미실시였던 것: 질문의 다른 절반(“NT probe의 이득이 층 선택·6-mer baseline 크기에 얼마나 의존하는가”)은 NT 임베딩이 캐시에 없어 이 기록에서는 실행하지 않았다. 나중에 

second_halves.md의 B①에서 임베딩을 새로 계산해(약 6분) 실행했다.

설정(고정): Wilk 2020 PBMC 하위표본 10,400세포, 기증자 13명, 기증자 단위 leave-one-donor-out이다. head는 로지스틱 회귀(C = 1 고정, 중심화·L2 정규화·표준화는 훈련 기증자만으로 적합)다. 다만 주 비교의 PCA(HVG, 50) 기준은 HVG 선택, 스케일, PCA를 held-out 기증자를 포함한 모든 세포로(라벨 없이) 적합한 transductive 설정이다(모듈 04 노트북 02와 같은 방식). PCA에 유리한 쪽이고, Geneformer 임베딩에는 이런 적합이 없다. fold별 적합은 민감도에서 따로 본다. 주 비교는 V2-104M <cls> L-2 vs PCA(HVG, 50), 거친 라벨 13종이다. 지표는 풀링 macro-F1(기증자 단위 부트스트랩 1,000회)과 기증자별 균형정확도다. 결정 규칙은 기증자별 균형정확도 Δ의 평균 ≥ 0.02, Δ > 0인 기증자 ≥ 9/13, macro-F1 Δ 구간 하한 > 0이다.

캐시에서 막힌 곳: pbmc_sub.h5ad에는 세부 라벨(cell.type.fine)이 없고 세포 이름도 cell0…으로 바뀌어 원본과 연결되지 않는다(obs: donor, disease, label, cell_type_cxg, n_counts). 노트북 04/01의 balanced_subsample(시드 0, 기증자당 800)이 결정적이라 그것을 wilk2020_pbmc.h5ad에 다시 적용했고, 기증자, 거친 라벨, cxg 라벨 10,400개가 전부 일치함을 확인한 뒤 세부 라벨 20종을 붙였다(스크립트가 assert). 새 다운로드는 없다. PCA(HVG)는 캐시에 없어 노트북 04/02와 같은 절차로 만들었다(7초).

결과 (거친 13종, 로지스틱 head):

주 비교 V2 − PCA: macro-F1 Δ −0.018 [−0.031, −0.009], 기증자별 균형정확도 Δ −0.036, 기증자 3/13이므로 지지되지 않는다. 대조인 사전학습 효과(V1 − V1 무작위 초기화)는 풀링 macro-F1 Δ +0.198 [+0.182, +0.223], 기증자별 균형정확도 평균 Δ +0.183, 13/13이라 '지지’다. 아래 Δ는 따로 적지 않으면 구간과 같은 풀링 macro-F1 Δ이고, 결정 규칙은 기증자별 균형정확도 Δ의 평균과 승수, 그리고 이 구간을 함께 본다.

민감도(한 번에 하나): PCA를 held-out 기증자를 빼고 fold마다 적합하면(중심화·L2 정규화는 주 비교와 같게 적용) Δ −0.015 [−0.031, −0.004], 균형정확도 Δ −0.030, 3/13이다. head를 kNN(k = 15)으로 바꾸면 Δ −0.036 [−0.064, −0.018], 균형정확도 Δ −0.090, 0/13이다(모듈 04 노트북 02의 zero-shot 수치 PCA 0.847·V2 0.811과 같다). 라벨을 세부 20종으로 바꾸면 Δ −0.079 [−0.097, −0.062], 균형정확도 Δ −0.103, 0/13이다(PCA 0.824, V2 0.744). 모두 지지되지 않는다.

읽기: 지도 head는 격차를 줄였지만(kNN −0.036에서 로지스틱 −0.018로) PCA 아래에 머물렀고, 라벨이 세분될수록 격차가 커졌다. 한 데이터셋과 head 하이퍼파라미터 1개(C = 1)의 결과다.

템플릿에서 바꾼 것: 시드 대신 기증자가 단위이고(분할은 결정적), Ridge/Spearman 대신 로지스틱/macro-F1을 쓴다. 음성 대조는 "훈련 라벨 섞기"이고, 무작위 초기화 대조는 캐시에 있는 V1 무작위 초기화 임베딩을 썼다.

주의: ⓪ 이 스크립트의 로지스틱 head는 max_iter=300이고 이후 

트랙 A~D의 “질문의 나머지 절반” 시험 실행 기록 (2026-11-09)의 C②③④ 스크립트는 max_iter=3000이다. 그래서 같은 PCA 기준선의 균형정확도가 여기서는 0.841, 거기서는 0.842로 적혀 있다(풀링 macro-F1은 둘 다 0.856; 판정에 영향 없음). 또 여기의 “PCA fold별”(0.835)은 PCA만 fold별로 적합한 것이고, 거기의 “엄격 fold별”(0.841)은 필터·HVG·스케일까지 훈련 fold로 적합한 다른 절차다. ① HVG 선택은 모든 세포로 했다(PCA를 fold별로 적합해도 남는 한계). ② 질병 상태가 기증자에 완전히 겹쳐 있다(COVID 7명, 정상 6명). ③ max_iter = 300에서 로지스틱 수렴 경고가 13번 나왔다. max_iter만 3000으로 올린 사본으로 다시 실행하면 경고가 없고 위 수치가 같았다(음성 대조만 0.068에서 0.069로). 경고는 joblib 작업자 프로세스에서 나오므로 스크립트 맨 위의 warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")와 무관하게 출력된다(리뷰 후 재실행에서도 13번). balanced_accuracy_score의 “y_pred contains classes not in y_true” 경고도 나온다. 한 기증자의 test에 없는 세포 유형을 예측한 경우이며, 균형정확도는 그 기증자에 실제로 있는 유형만 평균한다. ④ fold별 PCA도 HVG 선택은 전체 세포로 했다.

미실시(이 문서의 MVP에서): 새 데이터셋, 미세조정, scGPT 등 다른 모델. 이후 

트랙 A~D의 “질문의 나머지 절반” 시험 실행 기록 (2026-11-09)에서 라벨 입도(C①), 새 데이터셋(C②), Geneformer V1-10M 미세조정(C③), scGPT zero-shot 임베딩(C④)을 실행했고, V2-104M 미세조정은 Colab A100에서 따로 실행했다(C③-V2).

과제 1의 물음에 대한 관찰: "컷오프를 올리면 항상 어려워진다"는 가설은 이 설정에서 성립하지 않았다. ECFP4 RMSE는 컷오프 0.3에서 0.6으로 갈 때 0.906에서 0.827로 대체로 내려갔다(쉬워졌다). 0.3에서 0.4로의 오름(0.012)은 반복 sd 0.006~0.008 수준이다. 모듈 05 README의 값(random 0.750, 군집 0.4 근처 0.923; 반복 3회)과 같은 범위다.

템플릿에서 바꾼 것: Ridge·Spearman을 RidgeCV·RMSE로, 위치 블록을 Butina 군집으로 바꿨다. random 분할에는 군집 단위가 없어 부트스트랩 단위를 컷오프 0.4 군집으로 임의로 두었다(구간의 의미가 다른 칸과 완전히 같지는 않다). 노트북 05/01의 함수는 셀 안에 있어 import할 수 없으므로 balanced_group_folds, Butina, ChemBERTa 풀링 코드를 스크립트로 복사했다.

말할 수 없는 것: Lipophilicity 하나, 동결 임베딩 + 선형 head, 레이어·풀링 고정(마지막 층 평균)의 결과다. 다른 과제, 미세조정, MTR 변형은 다루지 않았다.

미실시였던 것: 과제 2(표기 증강 vs 정규화), 과제 5(거짓 음성 마스킹), 과제 3(다른 MoleculeNet 과제)은 

second_halves.md의 D②·D⑤·D③에서 실행했다. ChemBERTa 미세조정은 하지 않았다.

비용 주의: README는 트랙 D의 비용을 🟢로 적었는데, 이 MVP 하나가 약 14분이었다(대부분 ECFP4 2048차원 RidgeCV).

세 트랙 모두 새 다운로드 없이 캐시만으로 MVP를 끝까지 실행할 수 있었다. 막힌 곳은 하나(트랙 C의 세부 라벨)였고 결정적 재현으로 풀렸다.

템플릿 노트북 그대로는 안 되고, 구조는 옮겨 쓸 수 있었다. 바꾼 것은 데이터 로딩, 특징, 분할·단위(시드에서 염색체·기증자·반복으로), 지표뿐이었다. decide()와 “사전 등록 → 출처 → 점검 → 대조 → 민감도” 순서는 그대로 썼다. 트랙 B처럼 학습이 없는 비교에는 make_split/fit_predict 인터페이스가 맞지 않는다.

대조는 트랙마다 다시 정의해야 했다. 음성 대조는 B가 “그룹 내 점수 섞기”, C가 “훈련 라벨 섞기”, D가 "라벨 섞기"였고, 결정 규칙이 '지지’를 낼 수 있음을 보이는 양성 대조는 B가 “Evo2-7B vs TSS 거리만”, C·D가 "사전학습 vs 무작위 초기화"였다. 이 양성 대조를 넣지 않았다면 세 트랙의 "지지되지 않음"이 규칙의 편향인지 구분하지 못했을 것이다.

세 주 비교가 모두 "지지되지 않음"으로 나온 것은 질문의 선택 때문이기도 하다(FM이 강한 baseline을 이길지 묻는 질문). 새로운 결론이 아니라 모듈 03·04·05의 방향과 같다.

records.content:
커밋 1999904(Module 02 ESMFold Colab), f406cbd(모듈 05~07 Colab), df8e368(이 폴더)의 전체 diff를 Codex(gpt-6.1-terra)와 agy(gemini-4-argon-low)에 읽기 전용으로 보여 주고 검토받았다(Codex 6건, agy 8건). 지적마다 코드로 확인했다.

반영한 것

B 순열 p (Codex, 반영): 귀무분포를 점수와 무관한 순위(0…9)로 만들어 모든 점수에 같이 썼다. 점수마다 자기 값을 그룹 안에서 섞는 방식으로 바꿨다(위 표). p가 바뀐 것은 NT LLR 0.338 → 0.445, TSS 거리만 0.006 → 0.001이고 나머지 결과(AUPRC, 주·보조 비교, 대조, 민감도)는 그대로다. 모듈 03 노트북 02에도 같은 순위 기반 귀무분포가 있어서 같은 방식으로 고치고 다시 실행했다. 전체 변이의 p는 NT 0.34 → 0.41, HyenaDNA 0.53 → 0.63, Caduceus 0.92 → 0.93, TSS 0.006 → 0.001이었다. chr1 부분집합은 크게 달랐다. 직접 계산한 NT LLR은 1프레임 p가 0.035 → 0.109, 6프레임 평균이 0.138 → 0.289, 6프레임×정/역방향이 0.106 → 0.273이었고, 공개 NT LLR은 0.007 → 0.063이었다. chr1에서는 이전 p가 모두 지나치게 작았다(덜 보수적). AUPRC와 부트스트랩 구간은 그대로다.

C 주 PCA 기준의 transductive 적합 (Codex·agy, 공개 보강): 코드는 이미 그렇게 했고 주석에도 있었지만 README 설정 문단에는 없었다. 설정에 명시했다. 주 비교 자체는 모듈 04 노트북 02와 같은 설정이라 바꾸지 않았고, fold별 적합을 민감도로 이미 돌려 두었다.

C fold별 PCA 민감도가 두 요인을 바꾸고 있었다 (Codex, 반영): fold별 PCA에는 훈련 평균 중심화·행 L2 정규화가 빠져 있었다. 주 비교와 같게 맞추고 다시 실행했다(Δ −0.017 → −0.015, 결론은 같고 다른 모든 수치는 이전 실행과 같았다).

C 출처에 wilk2020_pbmc.h5ad 해시 추가 (Codex): 세부 라벨 복원에 쓰는 파일이다.

B MIN_GROUPS가 정의만 되고 쓰이지 않았다 (Codex·agy): assert를 넣었다. TraitGym 스냅샷 선택(iterdir()의 첫 항목)은 디렉터리만 정렬해 고르고 하나가 아니면 멈추게 했다(agy).

표기 (agy): C의 대조·민감도 Δ가 풀링 macro-F1인지 균형정확도인지 표시하지 않았고, B의 양성 대조는 염색체 평균 Δ에 풀링 구간을 붙여 적었다. 둘 다 구분해 적었다. B의 부트스트랩·순열 횟수도 적었다.

D 음성 대조의 평가 대상 (Codex): 섞은 라벨로 훈련하고 원래 라벨과 비교한 RMSE이다. 코드는 그대로 두었고(주석만 추가, AST 동일) 표 머리글과 주석에 적었다. 다시 실행하지 않았다.

반영하지 않은 것

decide()에서 ci is None이면 구간 조건을 면제한다 (agy): 템플릿 노트북의 설계이고 DECISION_RULE에 "구간을 계산할 수 있을 때"로 적혀 있다. D 스크립트는 MIN_TEST_GROUPS = 8이고, 스크립트의 앞부분만 다시 실행해 보니 모든 분할의 최소 test 군집 수가 162~840이라 이번 실행에서는 발동하지 않았다.

decide()가 len(deltas) < MIN_WINS를 유효 단위 하한으로 쓴다 (agy): 템플릿에서 물려받은 것이다. 이 조건에 걸리면 어차피 '지지’가 될 수 없고 라벨만 '판정 불가’로 달라진다. agy가 든 MIN_POS_CHROM=10 민감도 경우는 decide()를 부르지 않는다.

LogisticRegression에 random_state가 없고 경고가 숨겨져 13번 경고를 볼 수 없다 (agy): lbfgs 해법은 random_state를 쓰지 않는다. 경고는 joblib 작업자에서 출력되어, 리뷰 후 재실행에서도 ConvergenceWarning이 13번 보였다.

ESMFold 노트북의 weights_only 주석 (agy): transformers 5.22.1의 from_pretrained는 weights_only: bool = True가 기본이고 .bin은 torch.load(weights_only=True) 경로로 읽힌다(modeling_utils.py 확인). 주석은 맞다.

두 Colab 커밋(1999904, f406cbd): 두 리뷰어 모두 문제를 지적하지 않았다. 노트북의 출력은 비워져 있어 Colab 실행 수치는 리뷰어가 다시 계산할 수 없었다 — 이 부분은 독립적으로 확인되지 않았다.

English translation. AI-assisted translation of the 

Korean original. The Korean original is authoritative and may be newer. Links to pages without an English version open the Korean original.

The 

dry-run record ran only one question (the MVP) per track. This document records running, in the same way, the side that could not be run then, among the questions in the table of capstone README §2. The template structure is preregistration, provenance, data inspection, split and leakage, baselines, evaluation, controls, sensitivity, in that order.

What this record is

It is not a learner pilot. The people who made the course ran each one themselves, once. The times are single values measured on this Mac (MPS).

It is not a real preregistration. At the head of each script, the results the author had already seen (the related results of the module notebooks) were written. The decision rules and thresholds were fixed in the code before the run, but it cannot be proven that they were decided before the results were seen.

The only things newly downloaded were the 3 CSVs of D③ (after approval, 3.95 MB in total), the 1 H5AD of C② (after approval, 150 MB), the 26 scGPT source .py files of C④ (273,078 B) and the 3 files of the whole-human checkpoint (about 207 MB). The last two were also downloaded after approval. Everything else used only the caches. The embeddings and the fine-tuning fold results were newly saved in .cache/capstone_runs/ and excluded from git. Nothing was installed (pip install).

It received Codex and agy cross-review (see the “Cross-review” section at the bottom).

The results are not to be generalized to “ESM-2/NT/ChemBERTa/Geneformer are …”. Each row is one comparison with the data, the model and the head fixed.

Run: from the repository root, HF_HOME=$PWD/.cache/hf HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -I <script>. The run record (provenance.json) is written to .cache/capstone_runs/<RUN_NAME>/.

Verdict: The point-estimate ranking is the same at the three granularities (the order from top to bottom of the table above) and no pair flipped sign, so it is not supported. However, the PCA − V2 <cls> gap grew in the order coarse, cellxgene, fine as +0.036 [+0.018, +0.064], +0.080 [+0.063, +0.117], +0.074 [+0.056, +0.114] (fine − coarse +0.038 [+0.026, +0.064]). The V2 <cls> − V1 mean gap shrank to +0.260, +0.212, +0.230 (fine − coarse −0.030 [−0.053, −0.000]).

Caution in reading: The change happens all at once going from the coarse labels to cellxgene (19 classes), and hardly at all going from cellxgene (19 classes) to fine (20 classes). It is not a gradual effect of granularity but a difference of “13-class labels vs 19–20-class labels”, and the number of classes, the class sizes and the labeling criteria change together, so they cannot be separated. Each of the 20 fine classes falls within a single coarse label (0/20 exceptions in the hierarchy check).

Control: The pretraining effect (V1 − V1 random) is +0.198, +0.211, +0.215 with 13/13 donors, so it is ‘supported’ at all three granularities. The numbers of the coarse labels are the same as in module 04 (PCA 0.847, V2 0.811, V1 = 0.847 − 0.296 = 0.551).

Caution: As in module 04/02, the PCA baseline is a transductive setting that fits HVG, scaling and PCA on all cells (favoring PCA). There are classes that are absent in some donors: 6 in the coarse labels, 10 in cellxgene and 11 in the fine labels. The metric is computed from the pooled confusion, so it is defined, but it is not a per-donor value. There are 13 donors, and one dataset and one kNN each.

What was changed from the template: The unit is the donor (the same as the track C MVP). The decision rule of the primary comparison was newly defined not as “the number of donor wins” but as “a rank flip that takes the interval into account”. The win-count rule was used only for the pretraining control.

records.content:
Data (downloaded after approval): CELLxGENE “Cross-sectional” is the PBMC of an HIV-coinfected visceral leishmaniasis study (Commun Biol 2024, doi 10.1038/s42003-024-06225-2). 1 H5AD file, 150,017,626 B, https://datasets.cellxgene.cziscience.com/829fdf60-add0-4ca3-9b2f-dd86b3083885.h5ad, sha256 98a84e43ce2f… (the script asserts it), placed in .cache/singlecell/ (excluded from git). The license is as follows. The Zenodo record of the same study (10.5281/zenodo.10887674) is CC BY 4.0 (checked by API). The license notation of the CELLxGENE file itself could not be confirmed, and it is not redistributed. Nothing was installed.

Setup: The rank value encoding and the embedding extraction of module 04/01 were carried over as they are and applied to this data, and then the track C MVP was reproduced. The notebook functions cannot be imported, so they were copied, and the allow-list unpickler was kept. The primary comparison is Geneformer V2-104M <cls> L-2 + a logistic head (C = 1) vs PCA (HVG, 50) + the same head, leave-one-donor-out at the donor level, with the cell_type of the original data as the labels. There are three decision rules: the mean of the per-donor balanced-accuracy Δ ≥ 0.02, donors with Δ > 0 ≥ 70%, and the lower bound of the donor-bootstrap interval of the pooled macro-F1 Δ > 0. The author had already seen the same comparison (V2 < PCA) on the Wilk data, and fixed the setup before seeing the result on this data.

Data inspection: The original has 17,308 cells and 35,477 genes, raw.X is integer counts, and the gene IDs are Ensembl. There are 10 donors (8 patients and the healthy controls HEC1 and HEC2, 773–3,711 cells), and since each donor has only one disease status, the donor and the disease status cannot be separated (confounded; donors are nested within the disease group). A balanced subsample of 9,298 cells was made with at most 1,000 cells per donor, and then 15 cell types with fewer than 100 cells (500 cells) were left out of the evaluation (a rule fixed in advance, from 28 types to 13, 8,798 cells). 41% of the evaluation cells are is_primary_data = False in CELLxGENE. According to the official Census documentation, cells that duplicate another dataset in the corpus are False, and which dataset they overlap and whether it affects the results could not be confirmed⚠️. For some donors (0104, 0114, 0117, 0170), all the cells fall in this category. The tokenization results are as follows. V1 has 19,512 columns linked to the vocabulary, a median length of 1,487.5, and 14% of the cells truncated at 2,048 tokens. V2 has 19,263 columns, a median of 1,490 and 0% truncated. The maximum absolute difference of the padding-invariance check (alone vs batch) is 3e-8.

Results (13 classes, 10 donors, logistic head):

Primary comparison V2 − PCA: pooled macro-F1 Δ −0.041 [−0.061, −0.023], per-donor balanced-accuracy Δ −0.027, donors with Δ > 0 4/10, so it is not supported. The control, the pretraining effect (V1 − V1 random), is +0.141 [+0.124, +0.158], balanced-accuracy Δ +0.120, 10/10, so it is ‘supported’.

Sensitivity (one at a time): ① If PCA is fitted per fold (HVG selected with all cells), Δ is −0.031 [−0.055, −0.011] (balanced accuracy −0.015, 3/10). ② If PCA is fitted strictly per fold (gene filter, HVG, scaling and PCA all on the training folds only; a post-hoc analysis added after the cross-review), PCA is 0.807 (transductive 0.813) and V2 − PCA is −0.035 [−0.055, −0.017] (−0.023, 5/10). ③ With the kNN (k = 15) head it is −0.034 [−0.049, −0.018] (−0.033, 3/10; PCA 0.737, V2 0.704). ④ With V2 mean pooling it is −0.035 [−0.056, −0.017] (−0.025, 5/10). All of these are not supported.

Is it the same direction as Wilk?: It is the same. The supervised head on the zero-shot embeddings of V2 did not beat PCA (Wilk logistic Δ −0.018 [−0.031, −0.009], donors 3/13. Here −0.041, 4/10). The sizes of the gap cannot be compared, because the label sets (13 classes vs Wilk’s 13 classes/fine 20 classes), the platform (5′ vs 3′) and the number of donors (10 vs 13) differ. The gap of V1 against PCA (−0.190) is much larger than that of V2, and the pretraining effect (V1 − random) being positive is also the same as in Wilk.

Cautions and unverified: ① 15 of the 28 cell types were left out (because small types cannot be evaluated). The remaining 13 are large types, so this result does not apply to rare types. ② The labels are the automatic and manual annotations of the original paper and can be wrong. ③ PCA is a transductive setting fitted on the cells of all the donors, so it also sees the features of the held-out donor. In this run the difference from strict per-fold fitting was small, macro-F1 0.813 vs 0.807, and we do not go so far as to say that it generally favors PCA. ③′ The 13 evaluated cell types were defined as the types with 100 or more cells across all donors (including the evaluation donor). It is a population definition fixed by the number of labels, not by features or performance, but it is true that held-out label information was used. ④ The overlap with the Geneformer pretraining corpus could not be confirmed⚠️. It is a 2024 study, so it is likely not in V1 (pretrained in month 6 of 2021, a corpus of about 29.9 million cells, 561 public datasets), but for V2 (about 104 million cells, non-cancer) it is unknown. The model/dataset card gives the source only as “public data such as GEO and HCA”, and says the list of datasets is on the side of the Nature 2023 paper, but that list was not opened. ⑤ The logistic max_iter is 3,000, so the convergence condition differs from track C (300) (raising it to 3,000 in track C gave the same numbers). ⑥ It is a single run and there are 10 donors.

Computation: The embeddings took 128 seconds for V1, 127 seconds for V1 random initialization and 1,314 seconds (about 22 minutes) for V2-104M, and the total was 1,641 seconds (Mac MPS). The embeddings were saved together with the input keys in .cache/capstone_runs/h2_C_new_dataset_geneformer/. After the strict-PCA sensitivity was added, the script was re-run with the cached embeddings (106 seconds) and the earlier numbers were reproduced as they were.

records.content:
Setup (fixed): Wilk 2020 PBMC 10,400-cell subsample, leave-one-donor-out over 13 donors, 13 coarse labels (the same split as the track C MVP and C①). The model is Geneformer V1-10M (ctheodoris/Geneformer revision 1f7fbae4…; the same allow-list unpickler and rank value encoding as module 04/01). The configuration is the whole BERT backbone + mean pooling (excluding padding) + Dropout 0.1 + a linear head, and since V1 has no <cls>, mean pooling was used instead of the official first-token pooler. The hyperparameters were fixed and not tuned: 2 epochs, batch 32, AdamW (backbone 5e-5, head 1e-3, weight decay 0.01), 10% warmup + linear decay, the input truncated to the top-ranked 512 genes, no validation-based selection, per-fold seed = 0 + donor index. The decision rule is the same as the track C MVP, and there are two primary comparisons. One is fine-tuning vs PCA (HVG, 50) + logistic, and the other is fine-tuning vs the V1 frozen embeddings of the same 512-token input + logistic. The author had already seen the frozen-embedding results (V1 mean L-2 0.724, PCA 0.856) and fixed the setup before seeing the fine-tuning results.

Why V2-104M was not done: With the same setting it took about 17 minutes/epoch (about 9,000 cells) on this Mac (MPS), so 13-fold LODO was estimated at about 7 hours and it was excluded (a value measured once before writing the script, and the log was not kept). So the question “what if the better frozen embedding, V2 (0.838), is fine-tuned” cannot be answered by this section (it was later run on a Colab A100: 

C③-V2 below).

Data inspection: The median token length is 875, and 92% of the cells are truncated at 512 tokens (0% are truncated at 2,048). The newly computed 200 frozen embeddings of V1 at 2,048 tokens agreed with the module 04/01 cache with a maximum absolute difference of 1.19e-07, confirming that the tokenization and the vocabulary order are right.

Results (13 classes, 13 donors; the PCA and frozen-embedding rows use a logistic head, and the fine-tuning row uses a linear head trained together with the backbone):

Primary comparisons: ① Fine-tuning − PCA has pooled macro-F1 Δ −0.077 [−0.092, −0.056], balanced-accuracy Δ −0.075, donors with Δ > 0 1/13 (H2: 0.85 vs 0.83), so it is not supported. ② Fine-tuning − V1 frozen (512 tokens) is +0.107 [+0.086, +0.150], +0.123, 13/13, so it is supported. For reference, fine-tuning − V1 frozen (2,048-token cache) is +0.055 [+0.038, +0.095], +0.076, 13/13. Sensitivity: fine-tuning − strict per-fold PCA is −0.074 [−0.089, −0.054] (−0.074, 1/13), the same conclusion.

Controls: The positive control (the pretraining effect) covered only the first 5 donors. The pooled macro-F1 of the fine-tuning is 0.702, that of fine-tuning in the same way from random initialization is 0.269, the mean balanced-accuracy Δ is +0.392 and 5/5 are positive (the pre-specified rule was met). The negative control is 2 folds (C1, C2) of fine-tuning with only the training labels shuffled, whose balanced accuracy is 0.123 and 0.091. The uniform-guess baseline of the balanced accuracy is the inverse of the number of classes in that donor, so it is 0.083 for C1 and 0.091 for C2 (0.077 for a donor with all 13 classes). Since there are only two folds and the shuffled-label model is pulled toward the training marginal distribution, this baseline is an approximation. It does not contradict there being no signal, but it is not a tight test (it is far from PCA 0.79 and fine-tuning 0.76).

How to read it: Fine-tuning fills much of the gap of the V1 frozen embeddings. On the same 512 tokens it went from 0.673 to 0.779, higher even than the 0.724 of the 2,048-token frozen one. But it does not reach PCA in this setting (−0.077, lower in 12 of 13 donors). Truncating the input to 512 alone drops the frozen embedding from 0.724 to 0.673 (−0.051), so the possibility that the 512-token truncation lowered the ceiling of fine-tuning could not be separated in this run.

Cautions and unverified: ① Only V1-10M was used, there is 1 seed, and the hyperparameters were fixed and not tuned (the README strongly recommends tuning). Tuning may improve fine-tuning, so this value is a result “in this fixed setting”. ② V2-104M could not be fine-tuned in this section (it was run in C③-V2). ③ The positive and negative controls were run on only some of the folds (5 and 2). ④ The training loss fell to about 0.35 at epoch 2 (there is no validation fold, so overfitting was not measured). ⑤ The mean-pooling head differs from the official classification head. ⑥ 92% of the cells are truncated at 512 tokens. ⑦ PCA is a transductive setting (the same conclusion as the strict fit). ⑧ There are 13 donors and one dataset.

Reproduction and review history: 20 folds (13 + 7 controls) were run once (5,454 seconds in total; about 216 seconds per fold when alone, and 300–420 seconds in the intervals run concurrently with other jobs). With the final script that reflects the cross-review, the report was rebuilt from the cached fold results (55 seconds) and the numbers were the same. What was incorporated is as follows. The “500 tokens” notation in an output label was corrected to match the code (MAX_LEN = 512) (the typo remains in the log of the 1st run). The resume cache was moved to a directory of the settings·data fingerprint (after confirming that the settings, data hash, revision and package versions of the 1st run matched the new fingerprint, the files were moved). A PRIMARY marking error was fixed. The strict per-fold PCA sensitivity was added (post-hoc analysis).

records.content:
Why it is separate: C③ ran only V1-10M. What remained was whether fine-tuning V2-104M (0.838), whose frozen embedding is better, would exceed PCA. On the Mac (MPS) it is about 8 seconds/step, so only the training was run on a Colab A100 (user approval: A100, fp32), and the baselines and the report were made on the Mac. Script: 

h2​_C​_geneformer​_v2​_finetune​.py (stages check/bench/train/report).

Setup (fixed): The same data, split, hyperparameters and decision rule as C③, and the model (and what comes with it) and the pooling differ. V2 differs not only in the weights but also in the token, median and Ensembl dictionary (gc104M) and the special tokens, so the number of genes within the 512 tokens also goes from 512 to 510. The model is Geneformer V2-104M (the same revision 1f7fbae4…). The input is <cls> + the top 510 genes + <eos> = 512 tokens, and the configuration is the whole BERT backbone + the <cls> position of the last layer + Dropout 0.1 + a linear head (V1 had no <cls>, so it used mean pooling). 2 epochs, batch 32, AdamW (backbone 5e-5, head 1e-3, weight decay 0.01), 10% warmup + linear decay, fp32, no validation-based selection, 1 seed. There are two primary comparisons: fine-tuning vs PCA (HVG, 50) + logistic, and fine-tuning vs the V2 frozen <cls> + logistic of the same 512 tokens. The author fixed the setup having already seen the results of C③ (V1 fine-tuning −0.077), V2 frozen (4,096 tokens 0.838) and PCA (0.856), and fixed it before seeing the V2 fine-tuning results. What was seen before the main run was the A100 benchmark output (the step time and memory, and the training loss of the first few dozen steps of one fold), not an evaluation metric.

Data inspection: The token sha256 is the same on the Mac and the VM (4c43f5b3abea…; the input h5ad sha256 6ed51086… was also compared after uploading). The first 100 cells of the newly computed 4,096-token V2 frozen <cls> on the Mac agree with the module 04/01 cache with a maximum absolute difference of 0.00 (the check stage). The remaining cells and the provenance of the cache file are not re-checked in the report stage. 92% of the cells are truncated at 512 tokens.

Results (13 classes, 13 donors; the PCA and frozen rows use a logistic head, and the fine-tuning row uses a linear head trained together with the backbone):

Representation

Pooled macro-F1

PCA(HVG, 50)

V2 frozen <cls>, 4,096 tokens (module 04/01 cache)

Primary comparisons: ① Fine-tuning − PCA has pooled macro-F1 Δ +0.017 [−0.001, +0.041], balanced-accuracy Δ +0.021, donors with Δ > 0 8/13, so it is not supported. Of the three conditions only the effect size ≥ 0.02 was met; the number of wins falls short of 9, and the lower bound of the interval is at or below 0. ② Fine-tuning − V2 frozen <cls> (512 tokens) is +0.074 [+0.066, +0.094], +0.108, 13/13, so it is supported. For reference, fine-tuning − V2 frozen (4,096-token cache) is +0.035 [+0.022, +0.056], +0.057, 11/13 and supported. Fine-tuning − V2 frozen mean (512) is +0.087 [+0.076, +0.111], +0.124, 13/13 and supported. Sensitivity: fine-tuning − strict per-fold PCA is +0.020 [+0.000, +0.046], +0.022, 6/13, and not supported.

Per donor (PCA | V2 frozen 512 | fine-tuning): C1 0.79|0.75|0.88, C2 0.77|0.81|0.88, C3 0.87|0.68|0.84, C4 0.75|0.69|0.84, C5 0.79|0.67|0.80, C6 0.90|0.85|0.89, C7 0.91|0.72|0.80, H1 0.86|0.70|0.88, H2 0.83|0.80|0.86, H3 0.84|0.83|0.91, H4 0.92|0.76|0.90, H5 0.94|0.82|0.91, H6 0.78|0.73|0.84. Fine-tuning leads greatly in the donors where PCA is low (C1, C2, C4) and trails greatly in C7 (0.80 vs 0.91). The minimum rose from 0.75 to 0.80, but the maximum is higher for PCA.

Controls: The positive control (the pretraining effect) is, over the first 5 donors, a pooled macro-F1 of 0.770 for fine-tuning, 0.165 for fine-tuning in the same way from random initialization, and a mean balanced-accuracy Δ of +0.626 with 5/5 positive (the pre-specified rule was met). The negative control is 2 folds (C1, C2) with the training labels shuffled, whose balanced accuracy is 0.138 and 0.089 (the uniform guess based on that donor’s number of classes is 0.083 and 0.091; the same limit as C③, an approximate baseline since there are only two folds). The training loss of the random-initialization model is 2.20–2.24 at epoch 1 and 1.77–2.11 (mean 1.93) at epoch 2 over the 5 folds, and the balanced accuracy is 0.15–0.27. It falls far short of the pretrained model (loss 0.18, balanced accuracy 0.80 or higher), and is even lower than the pooled macro-F1 of 0.269 of the V1-10M random initialization. This control says only that “under the same 2-epoch budget, the pretrained weights make a big difference”. C1 of the negative control (0.138) is 0.055 higher than the approximate baseline (0.083). Because the shuffling was done only 1 time, the null distribution is unknown and it cannot be judged whether this is chance.

How to read it: When going from V1 to V2, the fine-tuning result moved from below PCA (−0.077, 1/13) to a level indistinguishable from PCA (+0.017, 8/13; 6/13 against strict PCA). By the pre-specified rule, “better than PCA” is not supported, and it is hard to say more than that the point estimate is positive (the interval straddles 0 and the number of wins is short). That fine-tuning is better than the frozen embedding of the same input is supported at 13/13 for both V1 and V2. The 512-token fine-tuning (0.874) came out even higher than the 4,096-token frozen one (0.838). But the two pipelines differ in more than the input length. Fine-tuning uses the last layer + a jointly trained linear head, and the frozen one uses the L-2 layer + centering·L2·standardization + logistic. So the effect of truncation, or its recovery, was not measured separately. Comparing the cost, fine-tuning is 351 seconds per fold on an A100 (13 folds about 76 minutes = 13 × 351 seconds), and PCA + logistic takes seconds on a Mac CPU.

Cautions and unverified: ① There is 1 seed. The verdict is on the boundary (Δ +0.021 against the criterion 0.02, 8 wins against 9), and it could flip either way depending on the seed and the hyperparameters. Multiple seeds were not run. ② The hyperparameters were fixed and not tuned, and there is no validation fold (the training loss is about 0.18 at epoch 2). ③ The pooling differs from V1 (V1 mean, V2 <cls>), so the difference from V1 to V2 cannot be separated into model size, the pretraining corpus, the pooling or the dictionary. ④ The training environment differs from the Mac. Colab was python 3.13 (confirmed in the session, not in meta.json), torch 2.14.1+cu130, transformers 5.22.1, scikit-learn 1.6.1 and an A100 in fp32, and the baselines and the report were made in the Mac .venv. The 512-token frozen embeddings were also computed on the VM (they were not recomputed on the Mac for comparison, and only the token hash was confirmed to be the same). ⑤ The controls are only 5 + 2 folds. ⑥ PCA is a transductive setting (the same verdict as the strict fit). ⑦ There are 13 donors and one dataset. ⑧ fp16 was 5 times faster in the benchmark (0.116 vs 0.580 seconds/step) but was not used, and whether the fp16 results would be the same is unknown. “fp32” means that autocast was turned off. Whether TF32 matrix multiplication was on on the A100 was not checked on the VM (the script does not touch the related setting). ⑨ The cache fingerprint binds the settings, the data and the tokens, but not the script version, the package versions or the frozen-embedding layer. In this run train was started once and finished without a resume, so there is no mixing, but if there had been a resume, the fingerprint alone would not detect it. ⑩ The speed, CU, Drive and benchmark numbers of this section were carried over from the session record and are not in the repository’s logs (progress.log, meta.json).

Computation and operations record: The whole training stage took 7,087 seconds (including 56 seconds of frozen embeddings; 20 folds = 13 + 5 random-initialization + 2 label-shuffled). The fold results are in a directory of the settings·data·token fingerprint (.cache/capstone_runs/h2_C_geneformer_v2_finetune/cache_32ac16273820/), and the report stage (Mac, about 60 seconds; run twice, 61 seconds and 59 seconds, identical numbers) reads them after confirming that the fingerprint and the settings match. The compute units used went from 531.98 to 518.72, that is 13.26 CU (A100 6.73 CU/h; including preparation, upload and waiting for shutdown. The preliminary benchmark took about 0.75 CU separately). Saving to Google Drive had been planned, but the CLI’s drivemount failed VM-side authentication even after the user’s approval, so it could not be used. Instead, the Mac downloaded the fold results every 5 minutes, and the VM was set to shut itself down 20 minutes after completion (in practice it was shut down manually right after completion). The 81 MB h5ad could not be uploaded in one go, so it was uploaded in 16 MB pieces and the sha256 was compared.

records.content:
Setup (fixed): The same data as C③ (Wilk 2020 PBMC 10,400-cell subsample, leave-one-donor-out over 13 donors, 13 coarse labels), and the same split as the track C MVP and C①. The primary comparison is scGPT (whole-human) <cls> embeddings + a logistic head (C = 1) vs PCA (HVG, 50) + the same head. The decision rule is the same as the track C MVP (mean per-donor balanced-accuracy Δ ≥ 0.02, donors with Δ > 0 ≥ 9/13, lower bound of the donor-bootstrap interval of the pooled macro-F1 Δ > 0). The author had already seen Geneformer V2 < PCA on the same data, and fixed the setup before seeing the scGPT results.

Source (downloaded after approval, nothing installed): The source is the 26 .py files (273,078 B; the MIT LICENSE file was checked) of commit cebd6fae… of 

bowang-lab/scGPT. They are placed in .cache/scgpt_src/ and loaded through sys.path without pip install (the script asserts the file count, the bytes and the hash digest). The checkpoint is best_model.pt, vocab.json and args.json of whole-human (about 207 MB in total, from the Google Drive folder in the scGPT README; the script asserts the sha256). The license notation of the checkpoint could not be confirmed (I checked again but found no license statement for the checkpoint in the README body. The repository’s MIT is a notation for the code, and the checkpoint is not redistributed). The weights are read only with torch.load(weights_only=True). The official embed_data assumes CUDA and os.sched_getaffinity (Linux only) and cannot be called as it is, so I used my own embedding loop with the same input configuration. The input configuration is <cls> + the genes whose value is not 0, with the values binned into 51 bins within each cell. If the number of tokens including <cls> exceeds 1,200 (that is, if there are 1,200 or more expressed genes linked to the vocabulary), a random sample with a fixed seed is drawn, and the last-layer output at the <cls> position is used. Here torch.backends.mha.set_fastpath_enabled(False) was needed (an operation of the eval-mode nested-tensor path does not exist on MPS).

Data inspection: The genes linked to the scGPT vocabulary (60,697) are 20,347 / 24,505 (83%), and the counts held by the linked genes are 99.0% of the total. None of the linked columns share a vocabulary id (checked separately). The cells where the token count including <cls> exceeded 1,200 (1,200 or more expressed genes) and a random sample was drawn are 2,247 / 10,400 (22%). Of the 163 checkpoint tensors, 162 were loaded with matching names and shapes (all with a value-identity assert), and the 10 model parameters that were not loaded are only the classification head cls_decoder.* (not used for the embedding). The only checkpoint tensor with no counterpart in the model is flag_encoder.weight (1 tensor).

Differences from the official procedure: The official function L2-normalizes the <cls> embedding row by row just before returning it, but here the pipeline common to all the features was used (centering on the training-fold mean, then L2). The official order (L2, centering on the training fold, L2 again) was also reported as a sensitivity, and the result was the same (below).

Primary comparison scGPT <cls> − PCA: pooled macro-F1 Δ +0.015 [−0.007, +0.033], per-donor balanced-accuracy Δ +0.000, donors with Δ > 0 6/13, so it is not supported. The macro-F1 point estimate leads, but the interval contains 0 and the balanced accuracy is a tie. The secondary comparison (same rule) scGPT − Geneformer V2 <cls> is +0.033 [+0.019, +0.049], balanced-accuracy Δ +0.037, 12/13, so it is supported. The control, the pretraining effect (scGPT − random initialization), is +0.315 [+0.299, +0.356], balanced accuracy +0.323, 13/13, so it is ‘supported’.

Sensitivity (one at a time): ① Gene-position mean pooling − PCA is +0.002 [−0.021, +0.023] (balanced accuracy −0.004, 4/13). ② The official order (L2 first) is +0.016 [−0.006, +0.033] (+0.000, 6/13). ③ If PCA is fitted strictly per fold (gene filter, HVG, scaling and PCA all on the training folds only), PCA is 0.854, differing from the transductive one (0.856) by only −0.002 [−0.010, +0.006]. scGPT − strict PCA is +0.018 [−0.008, +0.040] (+0.002, 5/13), and V2 − strict PCA on the same basis is −0.015 [−0.032, −0.004] (−0.035, 1/13). ④ If the head is changed to cosine kNN (k = 15), the direction changes. scGPT − PCA is −0.033 [−0.048, −0.012] (balanced accuracy −0.070, 2/13), and scGPT − V2 is +0.003 [−0.007, +0.027] (+0.020, 9/13). The PCA (0.847) and V2 (0.811) of the kNN are the same as the coarse-label values of C①. All the sensitivities are ‘not supported’ (including V2 − PCA in ③).

How to read it: On this data, the supervised head on top of the zero-shot <cls> of scGPT did not beat PCA and is at a similar level (the logistic has a point estimate of +0.015 with the interval containing 0, and with kNN it is rather below). It is better than Geneformer V2 (12/13 donors). That is, neither “FM beats PCA” nor “it always loses” holds, and the ranking changes with the model and the head. Per donor, scGPT is higher than PCA in C1, C2, C4, H2, H3 and others, and substantially lower in some, such as C7 (0.82 vs 0.91).

Cautions and unverified: ① The input configuration is not exactly the same as the official embed_data (“Differences from the official procedure” above; my own loop). ② args.json of the checkpoint records no_cls = true, no_cce = true and MVC = true. By their names they appear to mean that the classification and contrastive losses are turned off and the GEPC (MVC) decoder is turned on, but whether these flags were actually used that way in the real pretraining could not be confirmed⚠️. cell_emb_style is not recorded, so whether the <cls> position was used as the cell representation in the pretraining could not be confirmed either⚠️. What was narrowed down by re-checking on 2026-11-09 is as follows. In the source I fetched (model.py), when MVC is on, the input of the GEPC decoder is cell_emb, and with the default "cls" of cell_emb_style that is the output at the <cls> position. But there is no record that this checkpoint was trained with that default. The zero-shot tutorial README of the scGPT repository describes the original pretraining as “purely data-driven self-supervision (reconstruction of gene expression)”, which does not contradict the no_cls/no_cce records. So both <cls> and gene-position mean pooling were reported (the conclusion is the same), and the <cls> result is not interpreted as “<cls> is a pretrained cell representation”. ③ The 22% of cells for which a random gene sample was drawn used a fixed seed, so the change with other seeds was not measured. ④ The overlap with the pretraining corpus could not be confirmed⚠️. What was confirmed is as follows. scGPT whole-human is described in the README only as “33 million normal human cells”, and I did not find a list of datasets. The dataset of the same study (Wilk 2020) has been public on CELLxGENE Discover since 2020-09-28 (44,721 cells, containing both COVID-19 and normal labels; there are also non-primary copies in other collections), and this data includes the PBMCs of COVID-19 patients. It is possible that the cells of healthy donors were in the corpus, but this could not be confirmed. ⑤ The checkpoint scGPT_CP, which the repository provides separately for zero-shot cell embeddings, was not used. It is whole-human plus supervised training on the cell-type labels of Tabula Sapiens, and the README says it is the same as or better than the original. This run used the README’s default recommended model (whole-human). scGPT_CP is a model supervised with cell-type labels, so it differs in nature from this comparison, and using it would need an additional download (approval) and design. ⑥ This is a comparison of frozen embeddings. Nothing is said about a fine-tuned scGPT. ⑦ PCA is a transductive setting fitted on all the donors (③ above showed it is almost the same as the strict fit). ⑧ The 17% of genes not linked to the vocabulary (1.0% of the counts) were left out of the input. ⑨ There are 13 donors, one dataset and one logistic head.

Reproduction and review history: The whole run was done twice, and the two sets of embeddings were bit-for-bit identical (maximum absolute difference 0; MPS, same seed, same order). The 2nd run used the script that reflects the cross-review (a full check of the weights, a cache key that includes the input data hash, and the added L2-order and strict-PCA sensitivities). These two sensitivities are post-hoc analyses added after seeing the 1st results. The primary result numbers were the same as in the 1st run.

Computation (Mac MPS, run concurrently with the C③ fine-tuning, so it is not a standalone time): The embeddings took 564 seconds for whole-human + 553 seconds for random initialization (smoke test: 5 seconds for 128 cells, converted to about 7 minutes for the whole when run alone), and the total was 1,507 seconds.

Setup (fixed): Lipophilicity 4,200, scaffold split (the same function and seed as notebook 05/01), 5-fold × 3 repeats, frozen ChemBERTa-77M-MLM (mean pooling, last layer) + ridge. The compared variants are canon (trained only on normalized SMILES), avgK (the mean of the embeddings of K random notations of each training molecule) and rowsK (K notations augmented as rows), with K = 1/5/20. There are 3 test input conditions: normalized, 1 random notation per molecule (rand1), and the mean of 5 random notations (tta5). (c) “always normalize at inference” is canon training + normalized test. The random notations of training and test use different seed sets (20 sets for training, 5 for test).

ridge: alpha is chosen by molecule (scaffold)-level inner 3-fold on the same distribution as the input the variant is trained on (normalized, augmented rows, averaged rows) (augmented rows have several rows per molecule, so the leave-one-out of RidgeCV is leakage). The result of the canon variant is the same as notebook 05/01 (repeat 0: normalized 0.863, random notation 1.455, vs the notebook’s 0.863 / 1.448).

Decision rule: The primary comparison is rows5 vs canon (both with the rand1 test). It is ‘supported’ if all 3 repeats improve, the mean improvement is at least 0.10, and the lower bound of the cluster bootstrap interval is above 0. ‘Solved’ additionally requires “RMSE of the augmented head on random notation − RMSE of the normalized head on normalized input ≤ 0.05”.

ΔR@10 is +0.0073 for mask and +0.0042 for sampler.

Caution in reading: The Δ of mask is distinguishable from 0 by the seed sd (0.0007) and the interval (+15% in relative terms). But its absolute value is 0.002, which is the same size as the fluctuation of R@1 to 0.012–0.016 (width 0.004) when this script re-ran the 6 settings of notebook §7 (τ0, epochs, temperature fixed) with seed 0. There is no basis in this run for saying that “masking solves the false-negative problem”. R@1 is as low as 0.015, so the threshold of 0.01 was hard to reach from the start (it was not changed after seeing the results).

Why the effect is small (exercise ④; a hypothesis that was not verified†): First, false-negative pairs are only 1.6% of the pairs in a batch. Second, the bottleneck may be the frozen encoder and the small head, or near-duplicate texts in the gallery (even in the Pfam-grouped setting, texts are copied between families).

Controls: The positive control (alignment training vs shuffled pairs) is ΔR@1 +0.0141 [+0.0115, +0.0185], 3/3, so it is supported. For the negative control, the R@1 of the shuffled pairs is 0.0004 (chance 0.0007).

Caution: The sampler draws groups in proportion to size, so its training distribution differs from base (the details may not be the same as (b) of the exercise). The seeds change only the initialization and the batch order (the folds are fixed).

Data (downloaded after approval): SAMPL.csv (FreeSolv, 32,060 B), clintox.csv.gz (19,870 B) and bace.csv (3,897,767 B) from the DeepChem public bucket https://deepchemdata.s3-us-west-1.amazonaws.com/datasets/. The sizes were checked with HEAD before downloading, and the sha256 was pinned in the script. The license could not be confirmed (treated the same as notebook 05/01: not redistributed, used only as a local cache).

Setup: The pipeline of notebook 05/01 (6 representations × 3 splits × 2 heads, 5-fold × 3 repeats, 300 cluster-bootstrap resamples) was applied as it is to the 3 new tasks. The tasks are FreeSolv (regression, expt), BACE (binary classification, Class) and ClinTox (binary classification, CT_TOX; FDA_APPROVED was not done). The rule is that the improvement (positive = MLM is better) is positive in all 3 repeats, the mean is at least the minimum effect (0.05 times the y sd for regression, AUROC 0.02 for classification), and the lower bound of the interval is above 0.

Data inspection: FreeSolv has 642 molecules (0 invalid or duplicate), and of the 382 scaffold groups, 320 acyclic molecules are each their own group, so the scaffold split is close to random. BACE has 1,513 molecules (0 invalid or duplicate; positive 0.457) and has no time or date column, and the meaning of the values of the Model column (Test 1,265 / Train 203 / Valid 45) could not be confirmed. ClinTox went from 1,484 to 1,442 molecules (4 invalid SMILES; the 19 duplicate groups were all label conflicts and were removed; positive 0.064). The median nearest Tanimoto, in the order random, scaffold, cluster, is 0.52, 0.37, 0.43 for FreeSolv, 0.81, 0.72, 0.56 for BACE, and 0.51, 0.38, 0.32 for ClinTox.

④ Pretraining overlap: ChemBERTa-77M is known to have been pretrained on PubChem molecules († there is no model card). The molecules of these three datasets are likely to be in PubChem (especially FreeSolv and BACE), but this was not checked. Which direction and how much the overlap affects this comparison was not measured (that the overlap favors MLM is a hypothesis†).

Caution: The scaffold split is effectively close to random for FreeSolv (50% acyclic). This is a single run, and there is no per-representation tuning.

Setup (fixed): The promoter classification of module 03/01 (promoter_tata train 5,062 / test 212, promoter_no_tata train 6,000 (random out of 30,000) / test 1,372; the test is chr20 and chr21, and the chromosomes do not overlap with train). NT-500M mean embeddings (special tokens and padding excluded) are taken from 13 even layers among layers 0–24 and fed to a standardization + logistic probe, and C is chosen by chromosome-level inner 3-fold CV (AUROC) inside train. The baseline is k-mer frequencies (k = 3–7, dimensions 64–16,384). The training sizes are n = 500–6,000.

Decision rule: It is ‘supported’ if, for both tasks, ΔAUROC of (the layer chosen by train CV) − 6-mer is ≥ 0.01 and the lower bound of the test-resampling 95% interval is > 0.

Primary comparison: promoter_tata at layer 12 has Δ +0.001 [−0.030, +0.029] (NT 0.925 vs 0.925), so it is not supported. promoter_no_tata at layer 16 has Δ +0.010 [+0.004, +0.017] (0.947 vs 0.936), so it is supported. Overall, it is not supported. This agrees with the values of module 03/01 (tata layer 12 +0.001, no_tata layer 18 +0.010 [+0.003, +0.017]).

Dependencies:

Layer: Δ (fixed layer − 6-mer) is negative up to layers 0–8 in tata (−0.033 to −0.022) and layers 0–6 in no_tata (−0.022 to −0.002), and from layer 10 both become positive. The range of the per-layer Δ is −0.033 to +0.022 for tata and −0.022 to +0.012 for no_tata. By the selection method, in tata the CV chose layer 12 (Δ +0.001), but the last layer 24 is +0.021 and the test-oracle layer 22 is +0.022. In no_tata the CV layer 16 is +0.010, the last layer is +0.008 and the oracle layer 14 is +0.012. In tata, no layer has an interval that excludes 0 on the positive side (layers 2, 4 and 6 exclude it on the negative side; 212 test sequences).

Baseline k: The NT gain in no_tata shrinks to +0.024 at k = 3, +0.017 at 4, +0.014 at 5 and +0.010 at 6 and 7, but is supported at every k. In tata it is supported only at k = 3 (+0.037 [+0.004, +0.072]), the interval contains 0 from k = 4 (+0.010), and it is −0.011 at k = 7. The size of the baseline sets the size of the gain.

Training size n (layer candidates {6, 12, 18, 24}, compared with the 6-mer at the same n): The Δ of no_tata is +0.015 / +0.013 / +0.013 / +0.018 / +0.010 at n = 500 / 1,000 / 2,000 / 4,000 / 6,000, with no clear trend. In tata it is −0.012 to +0.010, and the interval excludes 0 nowhere (the train of tata has only 5,062 sequences, so the n = 6,000 row is in fact all 5,062). Boundary caution: At n = 6,000, if the layer candidates are limited to 4, the CV picks layer 18 and the Δ is displayed as +0.010, but the value before rounding is below the threshold (0.01), so it is ‘not supported’. With the 13 layers, on the other hand, the Δ of layer 16 was +0.010 (at or above the threshold), so it was ‘supported’. A comparison on the same task and the same data is split near the threshold by a difference smaller than one unit of the last rounded digit (the exact values were not recorded).

Controls: The positive control (the pretraining effect, NT − random-initialization NT, each with layers chosen by CV) is tata +0.128 [+0.070, +0.185] and no_tata +0.101 [+0.085, +0.120], so it is supported. The random-initialization NT is below the 6-mer (−0.128 / −0.091). In the negative control (training labels shuffled 10 times), the mean AUROC of NT layer 18 is 0.495 for tata (sd 0.051, range 0.430–0.595) and 0.504 for no_tata (sd 0.056, range 0.403–0.606), and the 6-mer is 0.495 / 0.497. A single permutation deviates from 0.5 by up to ±0.1 (in the first run I saw a single value of 0.606, and changed to 10 permutations).

Caution: The test has only 2 chromosomes, so the interval is a resampling of the test sequences (optimistic because it ignores the correlation of adjacent windows), and because it resamples with the CV-chosen layer held fixed, the variation of the layer selection is not in the interval. For no_tata only 6,000 of the 30,000 train sequences were used. NT was pretrained on the whole GRCh38 including the test chromosomes, so the comparison is not symmetric. The test-oracle layer is for diagnosis. Only a layer step of 2 and one mean pooling were examined. Assay selection rule (fixed before seeing the results): From the ProteinGym v1.3 reference table, among assays with length 100–250, no multiple substitutions (only single substitutions), and 500–4,000 variants, the first 3 in alphabetical order of DMS_id were chosen for each type. The 10 selected are as follows. 3 Activity (A0A1I9GEU1_NEIME_Kennouche_2019, CCDB_ECOLI_Adkar_2012, KCNE1_HUMAN_Muhammad_2023_function), 3 Expression (KCNE1 …_expression, NUD15_HUMAN_Suiter_2020, TPMT_HUMAN_Matreyek_2018), 3 OrganismalFitness (AACC1_PSEAI_Dandage_2018, CALM1_HUMAN_Weile_2017, CCDB_ECOLI_Tripathi_2016) and 1 Stability (ESTA_BACSU_Nutschel_2020). No Binding assay met the rule. Of the 13 Binding assays, the only ones with length 100–250 are B2L11_HUMAN_Dutta_2010_binding-Mcl-1 (170 variants) and RASK_HUMAN_Weng_2022_binding-DARPin_K55, and the latter has length 188 but contains 21,789 multiple substitutions, so it was excluded by the “no multiple substitutions” condition. The “binding” of the question could not be covered in this run. The rule was not changed after seeing the results. License: that of the individual DMS data is unconfirmed.

② Setup: An ESM-2 8M (last layer, embedding at the variant position) + ridge probe is compared with B0 (the mean of the nearest train position), B1 and B2 (position one-hot). The position-block split (about 20 blocks, block size = ⌈length/20⌉, test 20%) is run with 5 seeds, and the random split is used as an auxiliary. The unit is the assay, and the Δ of each assay is the mean of 5 seeds. The rule is mean Δ ≥ 0.02, assays with Δ > 0 ≥ 2/3, and the lower bound of the assay-bootstrap interval > 0 (per type there are few assays, so there is no interval).
